title: Forces and Newton's Laws
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Maths: Forces and Newton's Laws Worksheets
standard_text: Understand the concept of a force and Newton's first law; Newton's second law for motion in a straight line; weight and motion in a straight line under gravity; Newton's third law; equilibrium of a particle; connected particles and smooth pulleys.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level maths worksheets on forces and Newton's laws: F = ma, resistance, lifts, connected particles and pulleys, and resolving forces. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Draw a force diagram for each particle.
body_html:
How it works

Newton's second law: resultant force F = ma. Weight = mg. For connected particles, write F = ma for each particle; the tension is the same throughout a light inextensible string.

Example

Driving force 1500 N, resistance 300 N, mass 800 kg. Acceleration?

1200 = 800a

Answer: 1.5 m/s²

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting the weight.
  • Using the driving force instead of the resultant force.
  • Treating the tension as different on each side of a smooth pulley.

faq.a: The resultant force on a body equals its mass times its acceleration: F = ma.

faq.q: How do you solve pulley problems?
faq.a: Write F = ma for each particle and add the equations to remove the tension.
